email.body1:
Christopher, saw Alkira closed a $100M Series C and posted 1,261% three-year revenue growth on the Deloitte Fast 500.

Growth at that pace usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where good pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Alkira off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Christopher, quick follow-up for Alkira.

After a raise that size, the pipeline target tends to jump well ahead of headcount. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Alkira needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Christopher, last bit of proof for Alkira.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Alkira's reply rate likely compares to other high-growth startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Christopher, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything after a big raise, and that stretch carries its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to Alkira either way.
